morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 1
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 700 & SA 705 basics: forming the opinion, drafting, dating
🎬 After sir's Videos 1–3
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

CA Shreya, partner of SRK & Co., is finalising FY 2025-26 reports:

(i) Pragati Motors Ltd. (listed): closing inventory is overstated by ₹9.40 crore through wrong valuation of obsolete stock, overstating profit by the same amount. A material pending litigation of ₹14 crore (environmental penalties) is not disclosed. Management refuses to adjust or disclose. CA Shreya has sufficient appropriate evidence and concludes that the effects are material but not pervasive.
(ii) For Pragati Motors, the EQCR, CA Rohan, was on leave and completed his review on 28 May 2026. With the filing deadline near, CA Shreya signed and dated the report on 25 May 2026, arguing that "audit evidence was already complete; any EQCR point can be handled later".
(iii) Sigma Ltd.: CA Shreya will disclaim an opinion on the financial statements as a whole. Her manager suggests adding an unmodified opinion on the cash flow statement, as cash and bank were fully verified.
(iv) Orbit Robotics Pvt. Ltd.: there are three unresolved issues: (a) revenue of ₹8 crore from an undisclosed related party, (b) an asset with WDV ₹2.5 crore that could not be physically located, and (c) a subsidiary's qualified opinion. Taken together, they are so material and pervasive that the financial statements as a whole are misleading.

morning.question: Q1. What opinion should CA Shreya express on Pragati Motors Ltd. (item i)?
options: Adverse opinion
Unmodified, with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on the litigation
Disclaimer of opinion
Qualified opinion
morning.explanation: Misstatements (wrong inventory valuation and non-disclosure) that are material but not pervasive, where sufficient appropriate evidence exists, lead to a qualified opinion under SA 705.

morning.text:
2️⃣ Statements for Q2:
(i) The heading "Basis for Opinion" is amended to "Basis for Qualified Opinion".
(ii) For the inventory, the financial effect of the misstatement is described and quantified, if practicable.
(iii) For the undisclosed litigation, the nature of the omitted information is described.
(iv) The opinion paragraph uses "except for the effects of the matters described…".

morning.question: Q2. In drafting the Pragati Motors report (item i), which statement is correct?
options: (i) and (iv) only
(i), (ii) and (iv) only
(ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
morning.explanation: SA 705 requires the amended heading, a description and quantification of the financial effects of a misstatement, a description of the nature of omitted information, and "except for" wording in…

morning.question: Q3. Regarding the dating of the Pragati Motors report (item ii):
options: The date is valid if the EQCR's points are noted for next year
Cannot be dated before 28 May 2026 – report is not dated until EQCR is complete
The report must be dated on the AGM date
CA Shreya is right, as audit evidence was complete on 25 May
morning.explanation: Under SA 220 and SA 700, the report cannot be dated before the auditor has sufficient appropriate evidence, and for listed entities not before the EQCR is completed.

morning.question: Q4. Is the manager's suggestion for Sigma Ltd. (item iii) acceptable?
options: Yes, but only for the balance sheet
Yes, a piecemeal unmodified opinion is always permitted
Yes, if placed in an Other Matter paragraph
No – with a disclaimer on the FS as a whole, no unmodified opinion on a single statement
morning.explanation: A piecemeal unmodified opinion would contradict the disclaimer on the financial statements as a whole, so SA 705 does not permit it.

morning.question: Q5. What opinion is appropriate for Orbit Robotics Pvt. Ltd. (item iv)?
options: Unmodified opinion with KAMs on revenue and assets
Adverse opinion
Qualified opinion
Disclaimer of opinion
morning.explanation: When misstatements, individually or in aggregate, are both material and pervasive so that the statements as a whole are misleading, the auditor expresses an adverse opinion.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 1 Answers
📚 SA 700 & SA 705 basics: forming the opinion, drafting, dating

Q1 – (D) Qualified opinion
Misstatements (wrong inventory valuation and non-disclosure) that are material but not pervasive, where sufficient appropriate evidence exists, lead to a qualified opinion under SA 705.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.4.1 | Based on: RTP – May 2026, Q11(c)

Q2 – (D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
SA 705 requires the amended heading, a description and quantification of the financial effects of a misstatement, a description of the nature of omitted information, and "except for" wording in the qualified opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.8 (Form and content when opinion is modified) | Based on: RTP – May 2026, Q11(a)&(b)

Q3 – (B) Cannot be dated before 28 May 2026 – report is not dated until EQCR is complete
Under SA 220 and SA 700, the report cannot be dated before the auditor has sufficient appropriate evidence, and for listed entities not before the EQCR is completed. Significant matters raised by the EQCR must be resolved first.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 3.2 (Date of the auditor's report) & Ch 1, Para 3.6 | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 2, Q1(a)

Q4 – (D) No – with a disclaimer on the FS as a whole, no unmodified opinion on a single statement
A piecemeal unmodified opinion would contradict the disclaimer on the financial statements as a whole, so SA 705 does not permit it.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.7 | Based on: RTP – May 2024, Q3

Q5 – (B) Adverse opinion
When misstatements, individually or in aggregate, are both material and pervasive so that the statements as a whole are misleading, the auditor expresses an adverse opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.4.2 | Based on: MTP – Sep 2025 exam, Series 1, Q7

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 2
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 705: modified opinions
🎬 After sir's Video 4
👇 4 quick MCQs. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

morning.question: Q1. Management refuses to correct a misstatement that the auditor concludes is material but not pervasive. The auditor should express:
options: A qualified opinion
An unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
An adverse opinion
A disclaimer of opinion
morning.explanation: When misstatements are material but not pervasive, SA 705 requires a qualified ("except for") opinion.

morning.question: Q2. Ketan Exports Ltd.: PBT ₹2.10 cr, turnover ₹100 cr. An export receivable of ₹3.20 cr from a bankrupt foreign buyer is wholly irrecoverable (no ECGC cover). Management refuses to write it off. The appropriate opinion is:
options: Adverse opinion
Qualified opinion
Disclaimer of opinion
Unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
morning.explanation: Writing off the receivable would turn the profit into a loss. The misstatement is material and pervasive, so SA 705 requires an adverse opinion.

morning.question: Q3. When the auditor disclaims an opinion, the opening statement of the auditor's report is changed to say that:
options: "We have reviewed the financial statements"
"We were engaged to audit the financial statements"
"We have audited the financial statements"
"The financial statements have not been audited"
morning.explanation: In a disclaimer, SA 705 requires the introductory wording to say the auditor "was engaged to audit" the financial statements, and the auditor states that it does not express an opinion.

morning.question: Q4. After accepting an audit, management imposes a scope limitation and refuses to remove it. No alternative procedures are possible; possible effects of undetected misstatements could be material and pervasive. The auditor should:
options: Issue an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
Issue an adverse opinion
Issue a qualified opinion
Withdraw where practicable & legally possible; if not, disclaim an opinion
morning.explanation: SA 705: for a management-imposed limitation with possible material & pervasive effects, withdraw where practicable and legally possible; otherwise disclaim an opinion.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 2 Answers
📚 SA 705: modified opinions

Q1 – (A) A qualified opinion
When misstatements are material but not pervasive, SA 705 requires a qualified ("except for") opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.4.1 (Qualified Opinion) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 1, Q14

Q2 – (A) Adverse opinion
Writing off the receivable would turn the profit into a loss. The misstatement is material and pervasive, so SA 705 requires an adverse opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.4.2 | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 2, Q10

Q3 – (B) "We were engaged to audit the financial statements"
In a disclaimer, SA 705 requires the introductory wording to say the auditor "was engaged to audit" the financial statements, and the auditor states that it does not express an opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.8 (Form and content when opinion is modified) | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 2, Q8; MTP – Sep 2025 exam, Series 1, Q6(b)

Q4 – (D) Withdraw where practicable & legally possible; if not, disclaim an opinion
Under SA 705, for a management-imposed limitation with possible effects that are material and pervasive, the auditor withdraws where practicable and legally possible, and otherwise disclaims an opinion. Before withdrawing, the auditor communicates to TCWG any misstatements that would have led to a modified opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 5.5 and 5.6 | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 1, Q11

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 3
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 706: Emphasis of Matter & Other Matter paragraphs
🎬 After sir's Videos 5–6
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

MKR & Associates is finalising FY 2025-26 reports for several clients:

(1) Aster Ltd. (unlisted) early-adopted a new accounting standard, as permitted. This has a material effect on its financial statements and is fully disclosed in Note 3.
(2) Bharat Pumps Ltd. paid its managing director remuneration above the limits under Section 197 without the required approvals.
(3) Coral Foods Ltd. has no internal audit function. This is not mentioned anywhere in the financial statements. The engagement partner wants to "highlight it in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph". Management objects, and the audit found no evidence that affects the opinion.
(4) Delta Pharma Ltd. (listed) suffered a cyber-attack with a loss of ₹18 crore, already recognised in the accounts. The engagement team spent significant effort on it, and the partner considers it one of the matters of most significance in the audit.
(5) The audit team has prepared a checklist of what an Emphasis of Matter paragraph must contain.

morning.question: Q1. How should the early adoption at Aster Ltd. (item 1) be reported?
options: In an Other Matter paragraph
As a Key Audit Matter
In an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, with the opinion not modified
No reporting is needed, as it is a voluntary adoption
morning.explanation: Early application of a new accounting standard with a material effect is one of the SM's examples of circumstances where an Emphasis of Matter paragraph may be needed.

morning.question: Q2. Where should the excess managerial remuneration at Bharat Pumps Ltd. (item 2) be reported?
options: In the Auditor's Responsibilities section
In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section
In an Other Matter paragraph
In the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
morning.explanation: Under Section 197(16), the auditor reports on remuneration paid in excess of the limits in the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements. It is not an EOM or Other Matter.

morning.question: Q3. Is the proposed Emphasis of Matter paragraph for Coral Foods Ltd. (item 3) appropriate?
options: Yes, an EOM may highlight any matter the auditor considers important
No – an EOM can only refer to a matter presented or disclosed in the FS
Yes, but only with management's consent
No, because it must be reported as a qualified opinion
morning.explanation: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph must refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements. Absence of internal audit is not disclosed there and does not affect the opinion.

morning.question: Q4. How should the cyber-attack at Delta Pharma Ltd. (item 4) be reported?
options: Include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, as cyber incidents are fundamental by default
No reporting, as the loss is already recognised
Report it as a Key Audit Matter, since it was of most significance in the audit
Qualify the opinion
morning.explanation: A matter that required significant auditor attention and was of most significance is a KAM under SA 701.

morning.text:
5️⃣ Statements for Q5:
(i) A separate section with a heading that includes the term "Emphasis of Matter"
(ii) A clear reference to the matter and to where it is fully disclosed in the financial statements
(iii) A statement that the opinion is not modified in respect of the matter
(iv) Communication with those charged with governance about the expected EOM and its wording
(v) Additional information on the matter that is not disclosed in the financial statements

morning.question: Q5. Which items on the checklist (item 5) are correct requirements for an Emphasis of Matter paragraph?
options: (i), (ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
(ii), (iii) and (v) only
All of (i) to (v)
morning.explanation: An EOM must be in a separate section, refer clearly to the matter and its disclosure, and state that the opinion is not modified.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 3 Answers
📚 SA 706: Emphasis of Matter & Other Matter paragraphs

Q1 – (C) In an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, with the opinion not modified
Early application of a new accounting standard with a material effect is one of the SM's examples of circumstances where an Emphasis of Matter paragraph may be needed.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 6.2 – circumstances for EOM | Based on: MTP – May 2025 exam, Series 2, Q8; Suggested Answers – Sep 2025 exam, Q11

Q2 – (D) In the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
Under Section 197(16), the auditor reports on remuneration paid in excess of the limits in the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements. It is not an EOM or Other Matter.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 3.2 item 11 (Other Reporting Responsibilities) | Based on: MTP – May 2026 exam, Series 1, Q5

Q3 – (B) No – an EOM can only refer to a matter presented or disclosed in the FS
An Emphasis of Matter paragraph must refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements. Absence of internal audit is not disclosed there and does not affect the opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 6.2 & 6.3(b) | Based on: Model Test Paper 03, Q14

Q4 – (C) Report it as a Key Audit Matter, since it was of most significance in the audit
A matter that required significant auditor attention and was of most significance is a KAM under SA 701. An EOM is used only for matters not determined to be KAMs, and nothing here calls for a modified opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 6.2(b) & 4.3 | Based on: RTP – Nov 2024, Q2

Q5 – (B) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
An EOM must be in a separate section, refer clearly to the matter and its disclosure, and state that the opinion is not modified. The auditor communicates the expected EOM and its wording to TCWG. The paragraph refers only to information already in the financial statements, so (v) is wrong.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 6.3 & duty to communicate with TCWG | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 2, Q13

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 4
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 701: Key Audit Matters
🎬 After sir's Videos 9–9A
👇 4 quick MCQs. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

morning.question: Q1. CA Harsh audits the quarterly financial results of a listed company prepared under Regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR). Should he include Key Audit Matters in that report?
options: No – SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose FS of listed entities
Yes, SA 701 applies to any audit of a listed entity
Yes, SA 701 applies to audits of any entity
No, SA 701 applies only to review engagements
morning.explanation: SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities, or where the auditor decides or is required to communicate KAMs.

morning.question: Q2. In determining which matters required significant auditor attention, SA 701 does NOT require the auditor to take into account:
options: Areas of higher assessed risk of material misstatement, or significant risks
Matters already explained by management in the Directors' Report
The effect on the audit of significant events or transactions during the period
Significant auditor judgments on areas of significant management judgment / estimates
morning.explanation: The three considerations are higher-risk areas, significant judgments (including high estimation uncertainty), and significant events or transactions.

morning.question: Q3. A matter that gives rise to a qualified opinion is also among the most significant matters of the audit. In the auditor's report it is:
options: Omitted from the report
Described in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
Described in full in the KAM section
In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section; KAM section only refers to it
morning.explanation: KAMs are not a substitute for a modified opinion.

morning.question: Q4. The Audit Committee of a listed company asks the auditor not to include a major tax dispute, which he has determined to be a KAM, fearing negative publicity. The auditor should:
options: Still report it as a KAM – negative publicity is not a ground to omit it
Move it to an Other Matter paragraph
Qualify the opinion
Drop it, as the Audit Committee represents TCWG
morning.explanation: SA 701: a KAM is omitted only if law precludes it or, in extremely rare cases, adverse consequences outweigh the public-interest benefit. Bad publicity is not such a case.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 4 Answers
📚 SA 701: Key Audit Matters

Q1 – (A) No – SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose FS of listed entities
SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities, or where the auditor decides or is required to communicate KAMs. Quarterly results under Regulation 33 are outside it.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 4.2 (Applicability of SA 701) | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 1, Q2; also MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 2, Q1

Q2 – (B) Matters already explained by management in the Directors' Report
The three considerations are higher-risk areas, significant judgments (including high estimation uncertainty), and significant events or transactions. Disclosure in the Directors' Report is not a criterion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 4.3 (Determining Key Audit Matters) | Based on: RTP – Sep 2025, Q1

Q3 – (D) In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section; KAM section only refers to it
KAMs are not a substitute for a modified opinion. Matters giving rise to a modified opinion are KAMs by nature, but are reported in the Basis for Modified Opinion section, with a reference in the KAM section.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 4.2(b) and Illustration 2 | Based on: MTP – Sep 2025 exam, Series 1, Q11

Q4 – (A) Still report it as a KAM – negative publicity is not a ground to omit it
SA 701 requires each KAM to be described unless law or regulation precludes it, or in extremely rare circumstances where the adverse consequences would reasonably outweigh the public-interest benefits.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 3.2 item 6 (Key Audit Matters) | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 1, Q4(b)

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 5
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 570: going concern & its reporting
🎬 After sir's Videos 10–10B
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

CA Arjun is auditing Hari Textiles Ltd. for FY 2025-26. He notes the following:

• The company has made losses for three consecutive years and its net worth turned negative in March 2026.

• It has defaulted on two instalments of a ₹120 crore term loan.

• Its largest customer, which contributed 45% of sales, terminated its contract in January 2026.

• Management says the promoters will infuse ₹50 crore, but has produced only an unsigned letter of intent. Management has also prepared a 12-month cash-flow forecast.

• When CA Arjun asked management to extend its going-concern assessment to cover the full twelve months from the balance sheet date, management refused, saying "the auditor should do it".

morning.question: Q1. Suppose CA Arjun concludes that a material uncertainty exists but management's disclosure of it is NOT adequate. He should express:
options: An unmodified opinion with a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section
A disclaimer of opinion in all cases
Qualified or adverse opinion, stating the material uncertainty is not adequately disclosed
An unmodified opinion with a KAM
morning.explanation: SA 570: if a material uncertainty is not adequately disclosed, give a qualified or adverse opinion and say in the basis section that it is not adequately disclosed.

morning.question: Q2. Having identified these events, which procedure is NOT required by SA 570 at this stage?
options: Evaluating management's plans for future actions and whether they are feasible
Analysing the cash-flow forecast and the assumptions behind it
Requesting written representations from management about its plans
Issuing a disclaimer of opinion immediately, before evaluating management's plans
morning.explanation: When events or conditions are identified, the auditor performs additional procedures: evaluate management's plans, analyse forecasts, consider additional facts, and obtain written representations.

morning.question: Q3. Management refuses to extend its going-concern assessment. CA Arjun should:
options: Report the refusal as a Key Audit Matter
Include only an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
Document his request and give an unmodified opinion
Consider implications for the report – may lead to a modified opinion
morning.explanation: SA 570: if management will not make or extend its assessment, the auditor considers the implications for the report – usually a modified opinion (scope limitation).

morning.question: Q4. Suppose CA Arjun concludes that the going-concern basis is appropriate but a material uncertainty exists, and management's disclosure is adequate. The report will contain:
options: An adverse opinion
An unmodified opinion with the matter described only as a KAM
An unmodified opinion with a separate section headed "Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern"
A qualified opinion
morning.explanation: With adequate disclosure, the opinion is unmodified and the report includes a separate MURGC section that draws attention to the note and states that the opinion is not modified.

morning.question: Q5. If, instead, CA Arjun concludes that the company is not a going concern and the going-concern basis is inappropriate, but management still prepares the statements on that basis, he should express:
options: An adverse opinion
A qualified opinion
A disclaimer of opinion
An unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
morning.explanation: If the going-concern basis is inappropriate, the auditor expresses an adverse opinion. This applies whether or not the financial statements disclose the inappropriateness.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 5 Answers
📚 SA 570: going concern & its reporting

Q1 – (C) Qualified or adverse opinion, stating the material uncertainty is not adequately disclosed
If adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is not made, SA 570 requires a qualified or adverse opinion, with the basis for opinion stating that the uncertainty exists and is not adequately disclosed.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 6, Para 2 (SA 570 reporting chart) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 2, Q14

Q2 – (D) Issuing a disclaimer of opinion immediately, before evaluating management's plans
When events or conditions are identified, the auditor performs additional procedures: evaluate management's plans, analyse forecasts, consider additional facts, and obtain written representations. Reporting decisions come after this evaluation.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 6, Para 2 (When events or conditions are identified) | Based on: MTP – May 2026 exam, Series 2, Q4

Q3 – (D) Consider implications for the report – may lead to a modified opinion
If management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment when asked, SA 570 requires the auditor to consider the implications for the report, typically a modified opinion arising from the scope limitation.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 6, Para 2 (Management unwilling to make or extend its assessment) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2024 exam, Series 1, Q4

Q4 – (C) An unmodified opinion with a separate section headed "Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern"
With adequate disclosure, the opinion is unmodified and the report includes a separate MURGC section that draws attention to the note and states that the opinion is not modified.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 6, Para 2 and Ch 7, Para 3.2 (Going Concern element) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 2, Q14

Q5 – (A) An adverse opinion
If the going-concern basis is inappropriate, the auditor expresses an adverse opinion. This applies whether or not the financial statements disclose the inappropriateness.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 6, Para 2 (Use of going concern basis is inappropriate) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 2, Q22

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 6
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 720: other information
🎬 After sir's Videos 11–11B
👇 4 quick MCQs. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

morning.question: Q1. For an unlisted corporate entity, the auditor's report must include an "Other Information" section when, at the date of the auditor's report, the auditor:
options: Has obtained, or expects to obtain, the other information
Expects to obtain the other information
Has obtained some or all of the other information
Has obtained all of the other information
morning.explanation: Unlisted corporate entity: the section is required if the auditor has obtained some or all of the other information.

morning.question: Q2. If some documents of the annual report will be available only after the date of the auditor's report, SA 720 requires the auditor to:
options: Get a written rep that the final version will be given to the auditor before issue
Qualify the opinion
Disclaim responsibility for other information in all cases
Delay the auditor's report until all documents are received
morning.explanation: SA 720 requires a written representation that the final version of the documents will be provided to the auditor when available and before issuance.

morning.question: Q3. The Board's Report was received after the auditor's report was signed. Does the auditor have to read and consider it?
options: Yes – SA 720 also covers other information obtained after the report date
Only if the Audit Committee asks
Only for listed companies
No, since the auditor's report is already issued
morning.explanation: SA 720 sets out responses for a material misstatement in other information obtained after the report date, so the auditor must read and consider it.

morning.question: Q4. A listed NBFC's BRSR in its annual report claims "responsible lending with robust borrower screening", but the auditor found a lapse in screening during the audit. The auditor should:
options: Treat it as an SA 720 other-information issue and assess the lapse under SA 250 / controls
Ignore it, as BRSR/ESG disclosures are outside a financial statement audit
Immediately modify the opinion
Add an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, which fully discharges the responsibility
morning.explanation: BRSR in the annual report is other information.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 6 Answers
📚 SA 720: other information

Q1 – (C) Has obtained some or all of the other information
Unlisted corporate entity: the section is required if the auditor has obtained some or all of the other information. For a listed entity, it is required if the auditor has obtained or expects to obtain it.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 11.6 (Reporting) | Based on: MTP – May 2023 exam, Series 2, Q10

Q2 – (A) Get a written rep that the final version will be given to the auditor before issue
SA 720 requires a written representation that the final version of the documents will be provided to the auditor when available and before issuance.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 11.2(c) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 2, case facts to Q4–Q8 (Board Report not available at report date)

Q3 – (A) Yes – SA 720 also covers other information obtained after the report date
SA 720 sets out responses for a material misstatement in other information obtained after the report date, so the auditor must read and consider it.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 11.4.3 | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 2, Q8

Q4 – (A) Treat it as an SA 720 other-information issue and assess the lapse under SA 250 / controls
BRSR in the annual report is other information. A material inconsistency with the auditor's knowledge is dealt with under SA 720, and the underlying lapse is evaluated for compliance or control implications.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 11 & 11.3 | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 1, Q16

morning.text:
🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 7
📚 Ch 7 Reporting · SA 710: comparative information
🎬 After sir's Videos 12–12C
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

PNR & Co. is auditing FY 2025-26 financial statements for three clients:

(1) Finco Ltd. – PNR & Co. audited FY 2024-25 as well and gave an unmodified opinion. It now finds that development expenditure of ₹14 crore was wrongly capitalised in FY 2024-25 in breach of Ind AS 38. The error is material but not pervasive, and it has not been corrected by restatement or disclosed as Ind AS 8 requires. The company presents corresponding figures.
(2) Glow Ltd. – FY 2024-25 was audited by another firm, which gave an unmodified opinion dated 20 May 2025. Glow presents corresponding figures. The law does not prohibit reference to the predecessor's report.
(3) Kuber Tech Ltd. presents comparative financial statements. FY 2024-25 was audited by Gupta & Mehra LLP, which gave an adverse opinion because of a misstatement in trade receivables. The misstatement remains uncorrected in FY 2025-26.

morning.question: Q1. For Finco Ltd. (item 1), what is the reporting consequence for FY 2025-26?

Mention the matter only in an Other Matter paragraph
Qualified opinion on current-period FS, modified w.r.t. corresponding figures
Withdraw the FY 2024-25 report and issue a disclaimer
morning.explanation: When a previously undetected material misstatement in the prior period remains unaddressed, the current-period opinion is modified with respect to the corresponding figures.

morning.question: Q2. When corresponding figures are presented and there is no such issue, the auditor's opinion:
options: Refers to each period presented
Must always include an Other Matter paragraph on the corresponding figures
Refers to current period only; corresponding figures only in specified cases
Must include a separate opinion on the corresponding figures
morning.explanation: With corresponding figures, the opinion refers to the current period only.

morning.question: Q3. If Glow Ltd. had presented comparative financial statements instead of corresponding figures, the auditor's opinion would:
options: Refer to the prior period only
Refer to the current period only
Not refer to any period
Refer to each period for which financial statements are presented
morning.explanation: With comparative financial statements, the opinion refers to each period presented. This is the essential difference from corresponding figures.

morning.question: Q1. ABC Pvt. Ltd. is a wholly owned subsidiary of a listed company. Its paid-up capital plus reserves is ₹80 lakh, it has no borrowings, and its revenue is ₹6 crore. Is CARO 2020 applicable?
options: No, because it is a small company
No, because all of its financial thresholds are below the limits
No, because it is a private company
Yes – exemption is not available to a subsidiary/holding company of a public company
morning.explanation: The private-company exemption is lost if the company is a holding or subsidiary of a public company, whatever its capital, borrowings or turnover.

morning.question: Q2. In relation to consolidated financial statements, CARO 2020 requires the auditor to report:
options: Nothing, as CARO never applies to CFS
Only Clause 3(xxi): qualifications/adverse remarks in CARO reports of group companies
On all 21 clauses for every Indian subsidiary
Only on Clause 3(i) for the group
morning.explanation: CARO does not apply to consolidated financial statements except for Clause 3(xxi).

morning.question: Q3. A company revalued its land and buildings through a Registered Valuer, increasing their net carrying value by 18%. Under Clause 3(i)(d), the auditor must report:
options: Only if the change exceeds 25%
Whether done by a Registered Valuer, and the amount of change (as it is ≥10% of the class)
Under Clause 3(i)(c) instead
Nothing, as the valuation was done by a Registered Valuer
morning.explanation: Clause 3(i)(d) requires reporting on whether revaluation was by a Registered Valuer, and the amount of change if it is 10% or more of the aggregate net carrying value of each class.

morning.question: Q4. During physical verification, a machine with WDV of ₹2.5 crore could not be located. Management gave only an oral explanation that it is "out for calibration". Under Clause 3(i)(b), the auditor should:
options: Report the material discrepancy and whether it is properly dealt with in the books
Report only under Clause 3(ii)
Accept the explanation and report nothing
Report nothing, since ₹2.5 crore is small relative to turnover
morning.explanation: Clause 3(i)(b): report whether PPE was physically verified at reasonable intervals, whether material discrepancies were noticed, and whether they were properly dealt with in the books.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 8 Answers
📚 CARO 2020: applicability & Clause 3(i)

Q1 – (D) Yes – exemption is not available to a subsidiary/holding company of a public company
The private-company exemption requires the company NOT to be a holding or subsidiary of a public company, and also to be within the thresholds (paid-up capital and reserves ≤ ₹1 crore, borrowings ≤ ₹1 crore, revenue ≤ ₹10 crore). A subsidiary of a listed (public) company cannot use it.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 (CARO 2020 – applicability) | Based on: RTP – May 2025, Q4

Q2 – (B) Only Clause 3(xxi): qualifications/adverse remarks in CARO reports of group companies
CARO does not apply to consolidated financial statements except for Clause 3(xxi).
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(xxi) | Based on: MTP – Sep 2025 exam, Series 2, Q12

Q3 – (B) Whether done by a Registered Valuer, and the amount of change (as it is ≥10% of the class)
Clause 3(i)(d) requires reporting on whether revaluation was by a Registered Valuer, and the amount of change if it is 10% or more of the aggregate net carrying value of each class.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(i)(d) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 2, Q9

Q4 – (A) Report the material discrepancy and whether it is properly dealt with in the books
Clause 3(i)(b) requires reporting on whether PPE has been physically verified at reasonable intervals, whether any material discrepancies were noticed, and whether they were properly dealt with in the books.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(i)(b) | Based on: MTP – Sep 2025 exam, Series 1, Q5

📝 Case Scenario

CA Neha is the statutory auditor of Delta Agro Ltd. (a public company) for FY 2025-26. CARO 2020 applies. She notes:

(a) Physical verification of inventory showed discrepancies of 12% for fertilisers and 6% for seeds (aggregate for each class). Both have been adjusted in the books.
(b) The company had working capital limits of ₹8 crore from a bank, secured by current assets. Its quarterly stock statements differ materially from the books for two quarters.
(c) Statutory dues outstanding on 31 March 2026: GST of ₹2.0 lakh payable since 20 July 2025 (undisputed); PF of ₹1.5 lakh payable since 15 December 2025 (undisputed). Income-tax demand of ₹5.0 lakh is under appeal before the CIT (Appeals). For property tax of ₹1.2 lakh, the company has only made a representation to the municipal department.
(d) Cash loss of ₹2.4 crore in FY 2025-26 and ₹1.1 crore in FY 2024-25.
(e) CSR: ₹20 lakh remains unspent for a project that is not an ongoing project.

morning.question: Q1. Under Clause 3(ii)(a), which inventory discrepancy must be reported?
options: Seeds only
Fertilisers only (discrepancy of 10% or more for that class)
Both fertilisers and seeds
Neither, since both have been adjusted in the books
morning.explanation: Clause 3(ii)(a) requires reporting of discrepancies of 10% or more in aggregate for each class of inventory, and whether they have been properly dealt with. Only fertilisers cross 10%.

morning.question: Q2. On the working capital limits (item b), CA Neha must report under:
options: No clause, since the limits are from a bank
Clause 3(iii)(a), as loans are involved
Clause 3(ix)
Clause 3(ii)(b): whether quarterly statements to the bank agree with the books
morning.explanation: Clause 3(ii)(b) applies when working capital limits above ₹5 crore in aggregate are sanctioned on the security of current assets.

morning.question: Q3. Under Clause 3(vii)(a), what amount of undisputed arrears must be reported as outstanding for more than six months on 31 March 2026?
options: ₹1.5 lakh
₹2.0 lakh
₹3.5 lakh
₹4.7 lakh
morning.explanation: Only GST (payable since July 2025, so outstanding for more than six months at 31 March 2026) qualifies: ₹2.0 lakh.

morning.question: Q4. Under Clause 3(vii)(b), which dues are reported as "not deposited on account of dispute" with the forum?
options: Property tax ₹1.2 lakh only
Income tax ₹5.0 lakh (CIT Appeals) and property tax ₹1.2 lakh
Income tax ₹5.0 lakh before the CIT (Appeals) only
None of them
morning.explanation: Clause 3(vii)(b) requires the amount and forum of disputes. A mere representation to the department is not treated as a dispute, so the property tax is excluded.

morning.text:
5️⃣ Statements for Q5:
(i) Under Clause 3(xvii), CA Neha must report cash losses of ₹2.4 crore for FY 2025-26 and ₹1.1 crore for FY 2024-25.
(ii) Under Clause 3(xx)(a), she must report whether the unspent ₹20 lakh has been transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within six months of the end of the financial year.
(iii) Cash losses are reported only if the company also has a net loss under the Statement of Profit and Loss.
(iv) The unspent CSR amount must be reported under Clause 3(xx)(b) as it relates to a non-ongoing project.
Which are correct?

options: (i) and (ii) only
(i), (ii) and (iii) only
(ii) and (iv) only
(i) and (iv) only
morning.explanation: Clause 3(xvii) asks whether there are cash losses in the current and immediately preceding year and their amounts.

📚 CARO 2020: Clauses 3(ii) to 3(xx)

Q1 – (B) Fertilisers only (discrepancy of 10% or more for that class)
Clause 3(ii)(a) requires reporting of discrepancies of 10% or more in aggregate for each class of inventory, and whether they have been properly dealt with. Only fertilisers cross 10%.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(ii)(a) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, Q14

Q2 – (D) Clause 3(ii)(b): whether quarterly statements to the bank agree with the books
Clause 3(ii)(b) applies when working capital limits above ₹5 crore in aggregate are sanctioned on the security of current assets. It requires reporting whether the quarterly statements agree with the books.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(ii)(b) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 2, Q6

Q3 – (B) ₹2.0 lakh
Only GST (payable since July 2025, so outstanding for more than six months at 31 March 2026) qualifies: ₹2.0 lakh. PF has been payable for less than six months. Disputed and represented items are not undisputed arrears.

Q4 – (C) Income tax ₹5.0 lakh before the CIT (Appeals) only
Clause 3(vii)(b) requires the amount and forum of disputes. A mere representation to the department is not treated as a dispute, so the property tax is excluded.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(vii)(b) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, Q11

Q5 – (A) (i) and (ii) only

👇 4 quick MCQs. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM

morning.question: Q1. During the audit, the auditor has reason to believe that employees have committed a fraud of ₹1.20 crore against the company. He must first report it to the Board / Audit Committee within:
options: 30 days, seeking reply within 60 days
2 days of his knowledge, seeking their reply within 45 days
7 days, seeking reply within 30 days
15 days, seeking reply within 45 days
morning.explanation: Under Rule 13 for frauds of ₹1 crore or above, the auditor reports to the Board / AC immediately but not later than 2 days of knowledge, seeking a reply within 45 days.

morning.question: Q2. In the case above, the Board does not reply within 45 days. The auditor should:
options: Drop the matter
Wait until the Board replies
Forward his report to the Central Government with a note on the unanswered report
Report only in the CARO report
morning.explanation: If no reply is received within 45 days, Rule 13 requires the auditor to forward the report to the Central Government with a note on the report earlier sent to the Board or AC.

morning.question: Q3. The auditor's report on a fraud to the Central Government is sent:
options: By ordinary post to the ROC
Through the company's Board, in Form AOC-4
By e-mail alone to the RBI
In Form ADT-4 to the Secretary, MCA, sealed cover by RPAD / Speed Post + e-mail
morning.explanation: Rule 13 prescribes Form ADT-4, sent to the Secretary, MCA in a sealed cover by Registered Post A.D.

morning.question: Q4. During the audit, the auditor suspects a fraud of ₹60 lakh by employees against the company. Which statement is correct?
options: No reporting is needed, as it is below ₹1 crore
It is reported only in the CARO report
Reported to Audit Committee/Board within 2 days; company discloses it in the Board's Report
It must be reported to the Central Government in Form ADT-4
morning.explanation: For a fraud below ₹1 crore, the auditor reports to the Audit Committee or Board (Rule 13(3)), and the company discloses the nature, amount, parties and remedial action in its Board's Report.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 10 Answers
📚 Section 143 duties & fraud reporting

Q1 – (B) 2 days of his knowledge, seeking their reply within 45 days
Under Rule 13 for frauds of ₹1 crore or above, the auditor reports to the Board / AC immediately but not later than 2 days of knowledge, seeking a reply within 45 days.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12 – Duty to report on frauds (Rule 13) | Based on: RTP – Nov 2023, Q3

Q2 – (C) Forward his report to the Central Government with a note on the unanswered report
If no reply is received within 45 days, Rule 13 requires the auditor to forward the report to the Central Government with a note on the report earlier sent to the Board or AC.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12 – Rule 13(1)(c) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2024 exam, Series 2, answer to Q1(c)

Q3 – (D) In Form ADT-4 to the Secretary, MCA, sealed cover by RPAD / Speed Post + e-mail
Rule 13 prescribes Form ADT-4, sent to the Secretary, MCA in a sealed cover by Registered Post A.D. or Speed Post, followed by e-mail confirmation. It is signed on the auditor's letterhead with membership number.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12 – Rule 13(1)(d)-(f) | Based on: MTP – May 2026 exam, Series 2, answer to Q1

Q4 – (C) Reported to Audit Committee/Board within 2 days; company discloses it in the Board's Report
For a fraud below ₹1 crore, the auditor reports to the Audit Committee or Board (Rule 13(3)), and the company discloses the nature, amount, parties and remedial action in its Board's Report. CARO 3(xi) reporting also applies separately.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12 – Duty to report on frauds (B) | Based on: RTP – May 2024, Q10(b)

🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 11
📚 SA 299 Joint audit · SA 505 / SA 510
🎬 After sir's Video 16 (SA 299)
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

ABC Ltd., a listed pharma company (turnover ₹5,000 crore), has three joint auditors – PQR & Co., PK & Co. and XYZ & Co. They have divided the work in line with SA 299.

(1) PK & Co. learns that an employee has committed a fraud of ₹201 lakh against the company.
(2) Positive confirmation requests were sent to 100 suppliers, asking them to reply directly to the auditor whether they agree or disagree. Only 37 suppliers replied.
(3) Management refuses to let the auditors send confirmations to 37 debtors. The auditors find the refusal unreasonable and cannot get relevant and reliable evidence from alternative procedures.
(4) On valuation of inventories, PQR & Co. disagrees with PK & Co. and XYZ & Co. The majority insist that PQR & Co. sign a common report with their opinion.
(5) ZMR & Co., a new auditor of associate XY Pvt. Ltd., finds a material misstatement in the opening balances that affects the current year. Management neither corrects it nor discloses or presents it properly.

morning.question: Q1. For the debtors' confirmations (item 3), what should the auditors of ABC Ltd. do?
options: Report the refusal as a Key Audit Matter under SA 701
Only record the refusal in the written representation under SA 580
Communicate with TCWG and determine the implications for the audit and the opinion under SA 705
Report the refusal in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph under SA 706
morning.explanation: SA 505: if management's refusal is unreasonable and no alternative evidence is possible, communicate with TCWG and determine the implications under SA 705.

morning.question: Q2. On inventory valuation (item 4), PQR & Co. disagrees with the other two joint auditors. As per SA 299, PQR & Co.:
options: Must go with the majority opinion
May sign the common report and add its dissent in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
May issue its own opinion in the common report, highlighted by an EOM paragraph
Can issue a separate report; each report refers to the other in an Other Matter paragraph
morning.explanation: SA 299: a joint auditor is not bound by the majority. In disagreement it issues a separate report, and each report refers to the other under an Other Matter paragraph.

morning.question: Q3. For the uncorrected misstatement in XY Pvt. Ltd.'s opening balances (item 5), ZMR & Co. should:
options: Ignore it, as it was not the auditor for the previous year
Express a qualified or an adverse opinion, as appropriate, under SA 705
Only obtain a written representation; no reporting is needed
Only disclose it in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
morning.explanation: SA 510: if an opening-balance misstatement is not properly accounted for or disclosed, the auditor expresses a qualified or adverse opinion, as appropriate, under SA 705.

morning.question: Q4. For the ₹201 lakh employee fraud (item 1), what is PK & Co.'s duty under Section 143(12) and Rule 13?
options: Report to the Board/AC within 2 days; then send to the Central Government in Form ADT-4
Report only in the CARO report
Report only to the Audit Committee, since an employee committed it
Not report, since PK & Co. was not allocated that area
morning.explanation: Fraud of ₹1 crore or more: report to the Board/AC within 2 days of knowledge, seek a reply within 45 days, then forward to the Central Government in Form ADT-4.

morning.question: Q5. Only 37 of the 100 suppliers replied to the positive confirmations (item 2). As per SA 505, for the 63 non-responses the auditors should:
options: Treat the balances as confirmed
Perform alternative audit procedures to get relevant and reliable evidence
Qualify the opinion straight away
Ask management to confirm the balances in writing instead
morning.explanation: SA 505: for each non-response the auditor performs alternative audit procedures (e.g. subsequent payments, shipping documents) to get relevant and reliable evidence.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 11 Answers
📚 SA 299 Joint audit · SA 505 / SA 510

Q1 – (C) Communicate with TCWG and determine the implications for the audit and the opinion under SA 705
Under SA 505, when management's refusal to allow confirmations is unreasonable, or alternative procedures cannot give relevant and reliable evidence, the auditor communicates with those charged with governance and determines the implications for the audit and the opinion under SA 705. A KAM or EOM is not a substitute for a modified opinion.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 5 – SA 505 (management's refusal) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 1, Q4

Q2 – (D) Can issue a separate report; each report refers to the other in an Other Matter paragraph
SA 299 requires a common report, but where joint auditors disagree on the opinion or any matter, a joint auditor is not bound by the majority and expresses its opinion in a separate report. The reports refer to each other under the heading 'Other Matter Paragraph' as per SA 706.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 2, Para 5.4 (SA 299 – Audit conclusion and reporting) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 1, Q5

Q3 – (B) Express a qualified or an adverse opinion, as appropriate, under SA 705
Under SA 510, if the auditor concludes that opening balances contain a misstatement that materially affects the current period and its effect is not properly accounted for or adequately presented or disclosed, the auditor expresses a qualified or an adverse opinion, as appropriate, in accordance with SA 705.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 5 – SA 510 (audit conclusions and reporting) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 1, Q6

Q4 – (A) Report to the Board/AC within 2 days; then send to the Central Government in Form ADT-4
₹201 lakh is above the ₹1 crore threshold, so Rule 13 applies: the auditor reports to the Board or Audit Committee immediately but not later than 2 days of knowledge, seeking their reply within 45 days, and then forwards the report (with the reply or a note) to the Central Government in Form ADT-4. The duty applies to the auditor who comes to know of the fraud.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12 – Duty to report on frauds (Rule 13) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 1, case facts (fraud of ₹201 lakh)

Q5 – (B) Perform alternative audit procedures to get relevant and reliable evidence
Under SA 505, a non-response to a positive confirmation request gives no evidence. For each non-response the auditor performs alternative procedures, such as examining subsequent cash payments, invoices and shipping documents. A management confirmation cannot replace an external confirmation.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 5 – SA 505 (non-responses) | Based on: MTP – May 2024 exam, Series 1, case facts (37 of 100 suppliers replied)

morning.text: 3️⃣ Tess Products Pvt. Ltd. (FY 2022-23): turnover ₹35 crore (also ₹35 crore last year); paid-up capital ₹3.50 crore; working-capital loan ₹2 crore; registered as a 'Small Enterprise' under the MSMED Act. During the year it acquired all the shares of a Hong Kong company.

morning.question: Q3. Is CARO 2020 applicable to Tess Products Pvt. Ltd.?

No – it is a small enterprise under the MSMED Act
Yes – it is not a small company
No – it meets the private-company thresholds

morning.text: 4️⃣ Grow Ltd. has been sued by Glow Ltd. for ₹52 crore for allegedly stealing trade secrets through cyber theft. The legal opinion is ambiguous and there are case laws both ways. The financial statements are silent on the litigation.

morning.question: Q4. For Grow Ltd.'s silence on the ₹52 crore litigation, the auditor should:
options: Give an unmodified opinion
Treat it as non-disclosure of a material contingent liability – qualified opinion
Treat it as non-disclosure of a contingent liability – adverse opinion
Treat it as a missing provision – adverse opinion

📝 Case Scenario

CA Paras is auditing Meto Chemicals Ltd. (listed) for FY 2022-23. Revenue: ₹15,000 crore.

[A] Dues not deposited on account of disputes (₹ crore):
• Income tax, AY 2018-19, CIT (Appeals): 50.00 – no provision made
• Income tax, AY 2014-15, ITAT: 10.00 – demand stayed by ITAT; provision of ₹10 crore made
• PF contribution, FY 2017-18, High Court: 0.10 – no provision
• Property tax, FY 2015-16, High Court: 0.15 – no provision

[B] PPE ₹3,500 crore, Right-of-use (ROU) assets ₹750 crore (Ind AS 116 leases), intangible assets ₹42 crore.

[C] The Central Government has specified maintenance of cost records for its products, and a cost audit under Section 148(2) has been completed.

[D] Management's physical verification of inventory vs books (₹ crore): Raw material 1,000 vs 1,020; WIP 200 vs 220; Finished goods 2,000 vs 2,290; Stores & spares 150 vs 120.

[E] Two supervisors were dismissed for a ₹25 lakh fraud during the year; the full amount was recovered from them during the year.

1️⃣ Statements for Q1 (Clause 3(i)):
(i) The auditor reports whether proper records of PPE are maintained, including quantitative details and situation.
(ii) The duty on maintenance of records extends to ROU assets.
(iii) The duty on maintenance of records extends to intangible assets.
(iv) The duty on physical verification by management extends to ROU assets.

morning.question: Q1. For item [B], which of the statements on Clause 3(i) are correct?
options: (i) only
(i) and (iii) only
(i), (ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
morning.explanation: Clause 3(i)(a) covers records of PPE including ROU assets, and of intangible assets. Clause 3(i)(b) physical verification covers PPE including ROU assets.

morning.question: Q2. For item [C], what must CA Paras report under Clause 3(vi)?
options: Whether prescribed cost accounts and records have been made and maintained
Nothing, since the cost auditor has already reported
Only the qualifications in the cost audit report
Only on cost statements, not on underlying cost records
morning.explanation: Clause 3(vi): whether cost accounts and records prescribed under Section 148(1) have been made and maintained. A cost audit does not remove this duty.

morning.question: Q3. For item [E], is the ₹25 lakh fraud reportable under Clause 3(xi)(a) of CARO?
options: No – below ₹1 crore
Yes – report nature and amount, whatever the amount
No – the auditor did not detect it
No – the amount was fully recovered
morning.explanation: Clause 3(xi)(a) covers any fraud by or on the company noticed or reported during the year, with its nature and amount – irrespective of amount or recovery.

morning.question: Q4. For item [A], what total amount of disputed dues must be reported under Clause 3(vii)(b)?
options: ₹50.00 crore
₹50.25 crore
₹60.00 crore
₹60.25 crore
morning.explanation: All dues not deposited on account of dispute are reported with the forum: 50 + 10 + 0.10 + 0.15 = ₹60.25 crore. A provision or a stay does not remove reporting.

morning.question: Q5. For item [D], for which classes of inventory must discrepancies be reported under Clause 3(ii)(a)?
options: Finished goods only
Finished goods and stores & spares
Finished goods, WIP and stores & spares
All four classes
morning.explanation: 10% or more for each class, on the verified (adjusted) value: WIP 20/200 = 10%, FG 290/2,000 = 14.5%, stores 30/150 = 20%. Raw material is only 2%.

✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 13 Answers
📚 CARO 2020 – Clauses 3(i), 3(ii), 3(vi), 3(vii), 3(xi)

Q1 – (D) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
Under Clause 3(i)(a)(A), PPE includes right-of-use assets, so records of ROU assets are covered; Clause 3(i)(a)(B) covers records of intangible assets. Clause 3(i)(b) on physical verification of PPE also covers ROU assets. All four statements are correct.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(i) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, Q12

Q2 – (A) Whether prescribed cost accounts and records have been made and maintained
Clause 3(vi) requires the auditor to report whether maintenance of cost records has been specified by the Central Government under Section 148(1) and whether such accounts and records have been made and maintained. The existence of a cost audit does not remove this reporting duty; the auditor is not required to carry out a detailed examination of the records.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(vi) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, Q13

Q3 – (B) Yes – report nature and amount, whatever the amount
Clause 3(xi)(a) asks whether any fraud by the company or on the company has been noticed or reported during the year, and if so, its nature and the amount involved. There is no threshold, it does not matter who detected it, and recovery does not remove the reporting.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(xi)(a) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, Q15

Q4 – (D) ₹60.25 crore
Clause 3(vii)(b) requires disclosure of statutory dues not deposited on account of any dispute, with the amounts and the forum. All four items are disputes pending before an appellate forum or court: ₹50 + ₹10 + ₹0.10 + ₹0.15 = ₹60.25 crore. A provision in the books or a stay of demand does not remove reporting.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(vii)(b) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, case [A] (Q11)

Q5 – (C) Finished goods, WIP and stores & spares
Clause 3(ii)(a) requires reporting of discrepancies of 10% or more in the aggregate for each class of inventory and whether they were properly dealt with in the books. As per the ICAI key, the percentage is on the value after adjustment (physical verification): WIP 20 on 200 = 10%; finished goods 290 on 2,000 = 14.5%; stores & spares 30 on 150 = 20%; raw material 20 on 1,000 = 2%. So WIP, finished goods and stores & spares are reported.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 7, Para 12.1 – Clause 3(ii)(a) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2023 exam, Series 1, case [D] (Q14)

Q1 – (A) Qualified opinion

📝 Case Scenario

Jupiter Industries Ltd. is listed on BSE and NSE. M/s Pinnacle & Associates (engagement partner CA Rishi) is its statutory auditor for FY 2024-25. Those charged with governance are also involved in managing the entity.

• The firm had already issued the Limited Review Reports (LRRs) for Q1 and Q2.
• Before the Q3 review, management refused access to a critical overseas subsidiary's records, citing confidentiality with a JV partner. CA Rishi asked management to remove this limitation; they refused.
• After due procedures, the team concluded that the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be material and pervasive, so a qualified opinion would be inadequate.
• The firm proposed to resign on 25 November 2024, stating "professional pre-occupation" as the reason in its resignation letter.

morning.question: Q1. Management refused to remove the limitation. Since TCWG are also involved in managing Jupiter, CA Rishi's responsibility is to:
options: Communicate to TCWG and determine if alternative procedures are possible
Determine if alternative procedures can give sufficient appropriate evidence
Determine if additional procedures can give sufficient appropriate evidence
Get written representations and communicate to TCWG
morning.explanation: SA 705: if management refuses, communicate with TCWG unless all of TCWG are involved in managing the entity, and determine if alternative procedures are possible.

morning.question: Q2. Under the SEBI circular, what must Pinnacle issue before resigning on 25 Nov 2024 (Q1 and Q2 LRRs already issued)?
options: LRR for Q3, and then the audit report for the full year
Only the LRR for Q3
Nothing – Q1 and Q2 LRRs are issued, so it can resign now
LRR for Q3 only if the engagement terms require it
morning.explanation: 25 Nov is more than 45 days after Q2, so the next quarter's (Q3) LRR is required. Once LRRs for all three quarters are issued, the full-year audit report is also required.

morning.question: Q3. If Pinnacle had instead proposed to resign on 10 Nov 2024 (Q1 and Q2 LRRs already issued), what must it issue before resigning?
options: LRRs for Q3 and Q4
LRR for Q3 only
No further report – resigning within 45 days of Q2 needs only the Q2 LRR
The audit report for the full year
morning.explanation: Resigning within 45 days of a quarter-end requires only that quarter's report. 10 Nov is within 45 days of 30 Sep, and the Q2 LRR is already issued.

morning.question: Q4. If Jupiter were an unlisted company, was "professional pre-occupation" a proper reason in the resignation letter?
options: Yes – for an unlisted company, disclosing reasons is the auditor's choice
Yes – the clear-reasons requirement does not apply to unlisted companies
No – the auditor should clearly state the reasons in the resignation letter
No – reasons need to be given only to the incoming auditor
morning.explanation: ICAI announcement: the auditor of an unlisted company shall not cite 'professional pre-occupation'; the reasons must be stated clearly in the resignation letter.

Q1 – (B) Determine if alternative procedures can give sufficient appropriate evidence
SA 705 requires the auditor, when management refuses to remove a limitation, to communicate the matter to TCWG (unless all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity) and to determine whether alternative procedures can give sufficient appropriate evidence. Here TCWG manage the entity, so the remaining duty is to determine alternative procedures.

1️⃣ Uranus Pvt. Ltd. is an unlisted, partly-owned subsidiary of Saturn Ltd. (listed, Ind AS). All its members, including non-voting ones, were told in writing it won't present CFS; none objected. Saturn files CFS. Pluto Ltd., another subsidiary of Saturn, is an investment entity that measures its subsidiaries (Neptune 75%, Eris 60%) at fair value through P&L.

morning.question: Q1. Which statement about the consolidation of the Saturn group is most appropriate?
options: Uranus must prepare CFS as it is a subsidiary of a listed company
Pluto must consolidate all entities it controls
Saturn need not consolidate Pluto and its subsidiaries
Saturn must consolidate all, incl. Uranus, Pluto and its subsidiaries
morning.explanation: Uranus meets the exemption; investment entity Pluto measures its subsidiaries at FVTPL. But a parent that is not itself an investment entity (Saturn) consolidates all entities it controls.

morning.question: Q2. In the CFS audit report of WYZ Ltd., the division of responsibility between its auditor and the auditor of subsidiary ABC Pvt. Ltd. is reported in:
options: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph
The Key Audit Matters section
The Going Concern paragraph
An Other Matter paragraph
morning.explanation: Where the parent's auditor refers to other auditors' work on components in the CFS report, it is done in an Other Matter paragraph.

morning.text: 3️⃣ Titan Metals Ltd. holds 48% of MetalCore Innovations Pvt. Ltd., but under the shareholders' agreement it controls the composition of MetalCore's Board and so has power over its key financial and operating decisions. A trainee asks what the audit team must do about this investment.

morning.question: Q3. What must the audit team of Titan Metals do about the investment in MetalCore?
options: Nothing, since the investment was made earlier
Only audit the investment and related-party transactions
Audit the CFS, consider using component auditors' work, AND audit investment and related-party items
Only check the investment's carrying value
morning.explanation: Control of the Board makes MetalCore a subsidiary despite 48%. So CFS are needed (with component work under SA 600), along with procedures on the investment and RPTs.

morning.question: Q4. Next year Titan's stake in MetalCore (already a subsidiary through Board control) goes from 48% to 62%. The auditor's additional work is:
options: Start auditing CFS, as consolidation now begins
Audit the subsidiary's books to gain comfort
Choose between auditing the subsidiary or using another auditor
Only procedures on the increase in investment and its disclosures
morning.explanation: MetalCore was already a subsidiary (control via the Board), so consolidation is already being done. Only the change in stake and its disclosure need extra work.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 18 Answers
📚 Ch 13 – Group audit & CFS

Q1 – (D) Saturn must consolidate all, incl. Uranus, Pluto and its subsidiaries
Uranus is exempt from CFS: it is an unlisted, partly-owned subsidiary, its members were informed and did not object, and its ultimate parent files Ind AS CFS. Pluto, an investment entity, does not consolidate its subsidiaries but measures them at FVTPL. However, the investment-entity exception does not pass up to a parent that is not itself an investment entity. So Saturn consolidates every entity it controls, including those controlled through Pluto.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 13 – CFS exemptions (Companies Act & Ind AS 110) | Based on: Suggested Answers – May 2025 exam, Q3

Q2 – (D) An Other Matter paragraph
When the auditor of the parent uses the work of other auditors for components and refers to it in the report on the consolidated financial statements, the reference (including the extent of the components audited by others) is made in an Other Matter paragraph. It is not an EOM, KAM or going-concern matter.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 13 – Reporting on CFS (Other Matter) | Based on: RTP – May 2025, Q5

Q3 – (C) Audit the CFS, consider using component auditors' work, AND audit investment and related-party items
Control, not just shareholding, decides a subsidiary. Since Titan controls the composition of MetalCore's Board, MetalCore is a subsidiary even at 48%. CFS must be prepared and audited, and the auditor considers the financial information and the need to use a component auditor's work (SA 600). Audit procedures on the investment balance and related-party transactions are also needed. So both apply.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 13 – Subsidiary (control) & SA 600 | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 1, Q13

Q4 – (D) Only procedures on the increase in investment and its disclosures
Since MetalCore was already a subsidiary through control of the Board, CFS was already required and being audited. Increasing the stake from 48% to 62% does not change the status. The auditor only needs procedures on the increased investment and related disclosures (e.g. change in non-controlling interest).
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 13 – Subsidiary (control) | Based on: MTP – Jan 2026 exam, Series 1, Q14; Model Test Paper 03, Q11

morning.question: Q1. Mr. B (engagement partner) relied on the internal auditor's work on the Procure-to-Pay process without doing any procedure or keeping any documentation. As per SA 610:
options: He can use it, but only after evaluating that work, and he must document his evaluation
He can rely on it fully – no further procedure or documentation is needed
A statutory auditor can never use the internal auditor's work
He can use it after evaluating it, but documentation is not required
morning.explanation: SA 610: before using the internal auditor's work, the external auditor evaluates its adequacy and documents that evaluation and the procedures performed on it.

morning.question: Q2. CA Karan wants the client's internal audit team to give him direct assistance on factory wages. Before that, SA 610 requires written agreement from:
options: Only the Chief Internal Auditor
Only management of the company
No one – a discussion with management is enough
Both: management (team will follow his instructions) and internal auditors (confidentiality)
morning.explanation: For direct assistance, SA 610 needs written agreement from the entity (no interference, follow instructions) AND from internal auditors (keep matters confidential).

morning.text: 3️⃣ Copperbox Ltd. must appoint an internal auditor under the Companies Act. It gave the job to an employee who joined as a first-year architect. His reports are beautifully designed and even the Board praised them. The audit team wants to use his work.

morning.question: Q3. Can the statutory auditor of Copperbox use this internal audit work?
options: Yes – using it avoids doing the same work twice
No – competence and objectivity are lacking; the audit strategy must be reconsidered
Yes – the reports are well designed and praised by the Board
Yes – but only if the architect is in private practice
morning.explanation: SA 610: the external auditor first evaluates the internal audit function's competence and objectivity. A first-year architect lacks both, so the work cannot be used.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 19 Answers
📚 Ch 3 – SA 610: using the work of internal auditors

Q1 – (A) He can use it, but only after evaluating that work, and he must document his evaluation
SA 610 allows the external auditor to use the work of the internal audit function, but only after evaluating whether that work is adequate for the audit, performing procedures on it, and documenting the evaluation and conclusions. Blind reliance without documentation is not permitted.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 3 – SA 610 (Using the work of the internal audit function) | Based on: RTP – May 2025, Q3

Q2 – (D) Both: management (team will follow his instructions) and internal auditors (confidentiality)
Before using internal auditors for direct assistance, SA 610 requires the external auditor to obtain (a) written agreement from an authorised representative of the entity that the internal auditors will be allowed to follow the external auditor's instructions and the entity will not intervene, and (b) written agreement from the internal auditors that they will keep specific matters confidential.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 3 – SA 610 (Direct assistance) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 1, Q22

Q3 – (B) No – competence and objectivity are lacking; the audit strategy must be reconsidered
Under SA 610, the external auditor can use internal audit work only if the function has adequate objectivity, competence and a systematic, disciplined approach. An employee architect with no audit competence fails this test, however good the reports look, so the auditor cannot use the work and must plan his own procedures.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 3 – SA 610 (Evaluating the internal audit function) | Based on: Model Test Paper 03, Q9

📝 Case Scenario

Vistara Lifesciences Ltd. (listed pharma) is audited by Kavish & Co. for FY 2025-26.

• It capitalised ₹96 crore of drug development cost, saying technical feasibility is established. No one in the audit team has pharma or drug-approval expertise. The Finance Director says the company's own scientists have checked everything, so the auditor need not.
• Clinical-trial documents were given six weeks after they were asked for. The partner did not tell TCWG, since the documents finally came.
• ₹50 lakh was paid to a newly formed consultancy two days before year-end. The invoice only says "consultancy services". The consultant's address is the home address of a finance-department employee. The CFO says it is genuine.
• CA Nitin, a senior partner not in the engagement team, is the engagement quality reviewer. During the year he also helped prepare the firm's own GST returns.

morning.question: Q1. For the ₹96 crore capitalised development cost, Kavish & Co. should:
options: Do nothing more, as the Board has approved it
Rely on management, as feasibility is management's responsibility
Check the team's competence and, if needed, use an expert – not rely only on management
Always appoint an external expert for any R&D cost
morning.explanation: SA 620: if expertise in a field other than accounting/auditing is needed, the auditor decides whether to use an expert. Management's word alone is not enough.

morning.question: Q2. The six-week delay in giving important documents should be treated as:
options: Reportable only if the opinion is modified
Irrelevant, since the documents finally came
A significant difficulty in the audit that may need to be told to TCWG
A management matter outside the auditor's duty
morning.explanation: SA 260: significant difficulties during the audit, such as significant delays by management in providing information, are communicated to TCWG.

morning.question: Q3. For the ₹50 lakh consultancy payment, professional scepticism means the auditor should:
options: Treat it as fraud automatically
Keep a questioning mind and critically evaluate its unusual features
Accept the CFO's word, as he runs the finances
Do nothing, as it is below materiality
morning.explanation: Scepticism = a questioning mind and critical assessment of evidence. Unusual features (new vendor, vague invoice, year-end timing) need more work – neither blind trust nor automatic fraud.

morning.question: Q4. The consultant's address is a finance employee's home. This should mainly make the auditor:
options: Consider a related party, a fictitious vendor or another unusual link, and do more procedures
Take only a written representation from the CFO
Qualify the opinion straight away
Ignore it, as an address alone does not prove fraud
morning.explanation: A vendor linked to an employee is a red flag for an undisclosed related party or a fictitious vendor (SA 550 / SA 240). Further procedures are needed.

morning.question: Q5. CA Nitin also helped with the firm's own GST returns. As engagement quality reviewer, he:
options: Cannot act – only an engagement partner can review
Cannot do any other work in the firm for the whole year
Is automatically disqualified for doing any other work in the firm
Is not automatically disqualified; his eligibility and objectivity must be evaluated
morning.explanation: An engagement quality reviewer must be eligible and objective for that engagement. Unrelated internal work does not by itself disqualify him.

morning.question: Q1. As per SA 540, which of these accounting estimates is likely to have the HIGHEST estimation uncertainty?
options: Inventory obsolescence estimates made and updated often
An estimate using a well-known model with market-observable inputs
Outcome of a pending lawsuit against the company
Bad-debt allowance where past estimates proved accurate
morning.explanation: Judgments about the outcome of pending litigation have high estimation uncertainty. Frequent, routine or market-based estimates have low uncertainty.

morning.text: 2️⃣ Continental Foods: materiality was set at ₹40 lakh on budgeted revenue. Mid-year a big customer contract ended and actual revenue is much lower. The team keeps ₹40 lakh, saying it was already documented and communicated.

morning.question: Q2. Is the team's approach to materiality correct?
options: No – because budgeted figures can never be used
No – SA 320 requires revising materiality when new information would change it
Yes – if the original benchmark was reasonable at the time
Yes – planned materiality need not be revised once documented
morning.explanation: SA 320: the auditor revises materiality if, during the audit, he learns of information that would have led to a different amount initially.

morning.question: Q3. As per SA 530, if the auditor cannot apply the planned procedure or any alternative to a selected sample item, that item is treated as:
options: A misstatement in both tests of controls and tests of details
Neither – it is simply replaced by another item
A deviation in both tests
A deviation (test of controls) or a misstatement (test of details)
morning.explanation: SA 530: an item that cannot be tested is treated as a deviation from the control (tests of controls) or as a misstatement (tests of details).

morning.text: 4️⃣ Speak Ltd. shows commission of ₹2 crore for October. The auditor traces how this line item is initiated, recorded, approved, posted and reported, and finds a ₹1.5 lakh difference between the commission software (source) and SAP (destination).

morning.question: Q4. What kind of risk assessment is this?
options: Evaluation of risks and controls at process level
Indirect entity-level control evaluation
No risk assessment at all
Direct entity-level control evaluation
morning.explanation: Walking through how a line item flows from initiation to reporting, and testing the source-to-ledger link, is a process-level evaluation of risks and controls.
