🟦 CA FINAL AUDIT DAILY MCQ – Day 22
📚 Ch 3/5/6 – Confirmations, misstatements & subsequent events
🎬 After sir's Ch 3 Videos 4–4B (SA 450) + revision
👇 1 case, followed by 5 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

Kaveri & Associates audit Campaign Textiles Ltd. (unlisted exporter) for FY 2025-26.

• Positive confirmations were sent directly to 40 large customers. 25 replied directly. For the other 15, audit senior CA Rishu asked the company's accounts team to follow up and pass on any replies, as "they know the customers better".
• Three uncorrected misstatements were found: ₹35 lakh (revenue/expense classification), ₹20 lakh and ₹18 lakh (two expense heads). Each was judged immaterial when found, so none was put in the summary of uncorrected misstatements. Performance materiality: ₹70 lakh.
• After year-end, but before the report date, a major customer (15% of receivables) filed for insolvency. Its liquidity crisis had existed for a long time before year-end. Management refuses to increase the provision.

morning.question: Q1. Is routing the 15 pending confirmations through the company's accounts team acceptable under SA 505?
options: No – the auditor must control the confirmation process; this makes the evidence unreliable
Yes – SA 505 covers only the first request
Yes – the company has better customer relations
No – but only because over 25% were followed up by the client
morning.explanation: SA 505 requires the auditor to keep control over confirmation requests and replies. Follow-up through the client compromises reliability.

morning.question: Q2. For those 15 customer balances, the auditor should now:
options: Drop them and conclude on the 25 direct replies
Do alternative procedures – later receipts, shipping documents, invoices
Make an extra bad-debt provision for them
Treat them as confirmed if replies come via the accounts team
morning.explanation: When confirmation fails, SA 505 requires alternative procedures such as subsequent cash receipts, shipping documents and sales invoices.

morning.question: Q3. How should the three misstatements (₹35 lakh, ₹20 lakh, ₹18 lakh) be dealt with under SA 450?
options: Ignore them – each was immaterial when found
Accumulate only if they relate to the same account
Accumulate them (unless clearly trivial) and evaluate individually AND in aggregate
Never aggregate items from different procedures
morning.explanation: SA 450: accumulate all misstatements except clearly trivial ones and evaluate them individually and in aggregate. Together = ₹73 lakh, above PM of ₹70 lakh.

morning.question: Q4. Under SA 560, the customer's insolvency is:
options: A non-adjusting event needing only disclosure
An adjusting event, but the auditor need not ask for adjustment
A non-adjusting event, as the filing came after year-end
An adjusting event – the crisis existed at year-end, so the provision must be adjusted
morning.explanation: The condition (liquidity crisis) existed at the balance sheet date; the insolvency only confirms it. So it is an adjusting event.

morning.question: Q5. Management refuses to adjust, and the misstatement is material but not pervasive. The opinion is:
options: Disclaimer
Qualified
Unmodified with an Emphasis of Matter
Adverse
morning.explanation: A material but not pervasive misstatement that management will not correct leads to a qualified opinion under SA 705.

Q1 – (A) No – the auditor must control the confirmation process; this makes the evidence unreliable
SA 505 requires the auditor to keep control over confirmation requests and replies. Follow-up through the client compromises reliability.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 5 – SA 505 | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 1, Q10

Q2 – (B) Do alternative procedures – later receipts, shipping documents, invoices
When confirmation fails, SA 505 requires alternative procedures such as subsequent cash receipts, shipping documents and sales invoices.

Ignore them, as they are below materiality

Pick another sample until no errors appear

📚 Ch 19 – Misconduct & disciplinary procedure
🎬 After sir's Ch 19 Videos 7–8 (Disciplinary Procedure, Schedules)
👇 1 case, followed by 4 polls. ⏰ Full answers at 8:30 PM
🎯 Quiz mode: vote once and see instantly if you are right – only you can see it. Tap 💡 for why.

📝 Case Scenario

Pitch Pvt. Ltd. asked CA Hitesh, a practising CA, to digitally sign and upload on the ROC portal the form for the resignation of one of its directors, Mr. Mohit. Mr. Mohit's signature on the resignation letter had been copied and pasted by another director. CA Hitesh did not verify the letter, signed the form digitally and uploaded it.

A complaint reached the Director (Discipline). On investigation he was found guilty, and a penalty was imposed under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.

morning.question: Q1. Signing and uploading the form without checking the authenticity of the resignation letter is misconduct under:
options: Clause (2), Part I, Second Schedule
Clause (7), Part I, First Schedule
Clause (7), Part I, Second Schedule – gross negligence
Clause (5), Part I, First Schedule
morning.explanation: Certifying/uploading a document without verifying it is gross negligence in professional duties – Clause (7) of Part I of the Second Schedule.

morning.question: Q2. Since the misconduct falls under the Second Schedule, the case is placed before the:
options: Disciplinary Committee
Appellate Authority
High Court
Board of Discipline
morning.explanation: Director (Discipline): First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline; Second Schedule (or both) go to the Disciplinary Committee.

morning.question: Q3. What is the MINIMUM punishment the Disciplinary Committee could impose on CA Hitesh?
options: Suspension for up to 3 months
Removal of name and fine up to ₹5 lakh
Warning and fine up to ₹50,000
Reprimand
morning.explanation: The Disciplinary Committee can reprimand, remove the name (permanently or for any period) and/or fine up to ₹5 lakh. The lightest is a reprimand.

morning.question: Q4. Compared with the Disciplinary Committee, what is the maximum the Board of Discipline can do (First Schedule cases)?
options: Remove name permanently and fine up to ₹5 lakh
Reprimand, remove name up to 3 months, fine up to ₹1 lakh
Fine up to ₹5 lakh but no removal
Only reprimand
morning.explanation: Board of Discipline: reprimand, removal up to 3 months, fine up to ₹1 lakh. Disciplinary Committee: removal for any period, fine up to ₹5 lakh.

evening:
✅ CA FINAL AUDIT – Day 24 Answers
📚 Ch 19 – Misconduct & disciplinary procedure

Q1 – (C) Clause (7), Part I, Second Schedule – gross negligence
Certifying/uploading a document without verifying it is gross negligence in professional duties – Clause (7) of Part I of the Second Schedule.
📖 ICAI SM (May 27), Ch 19 – Second Schedule, Part I, Clause (7) | Based on: MTP – Nov 2026 exam, Series 1, Q7

Q2 – (A) Disciplinary Committee
Director (Discipline): First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline; Second Schedule (or both) go to the Disciplinary Committee.

📝 Case Scenario

M/s AIM & Co., a new CA firm, immediately accepted the statutory audit of DM Crackers Ltd. without following the required procedures (no communication with the previous auditor).

(I) The auditors asked for the previous year's financials and the transactions up to 25 May of the current year. Management said both were "out of scope" and gave them only after repeated requests.
(II) Partner Mr. Shyam later resigned from the firm and joined a manufacturing company through a recruitment agency. The agency billed 0.2% of his CTC, which he agreed to pay (a friend later gave him a full discount).
(III) Partner Mr. Ghanshyam acts as a Registration Authority for obtaining digital signatures for clients.

morning.question: Q1. On item (I), which is correct?
options: Only the previous year's financials can be asked for
Management is right – both are out of scope
The auditors have the right to ask for both; management's 'out of scope' stand is wrong
Both sides have equal rights to ask and to refuse
morning.explanation: The auditor has a right of access to books and information needed – including prior-year figures and post-balance-sheet transactions (subsequent events).

morning.question: Q2. Is AIM & Co. guilty of misconduct for accepting the audit this way?
options: Yes – Clause (8), Part I, First Schedule (no prior communication with previous auditor)
No – no provision is violated
Yes – Clause (1), Part I, Second Schedule
Yes – Clause (2), Part II, Second Schedule
morning.explanation: Clause (8): a member must communicate in writing with the previous auditor BEFORE accepting the position. Not doing so is misconduct.

morning.question: Q3. Mr. Shyam (now a member in service) agreed to pay the agency 0.2% of his CTC. Is he guilty?
options: Yes – Clause (1), Part I, First Schedule
Yes – Clause (1), Part II, First Schedule
No – he got a full discount
Yes – Clause (2), Part II, Second Schedule
morning.explanation: A member in service who pays or agrees to pay any share of his emoluments to another person is guilty under Clause (1) of Part II, First Schedule. Agreeing is enough.

morning.question: Q4. Is Mr. Ghanshyam guilty for acting as a Registration Authority for clients' digital signatures?
options: Yes – Part III, Second Schedule
Yes – Clause (11), Part I, First Schedule
Yes – Clause (1), Part II, Second Schedule
No – a CA in practice may act as Registration Authority for DSCs
morning.explanation: As per ESB decisions, a CA in practice may engage himself as Registration Authority for obtaining digital signatures for clients.

📝 Case Scenario

PO & Associates (partners CA P and CA O), Chennai, audit Ring Ltd.

• Ring Ltd.'s internal auditor CA Tom is asked to give direct assistance in (a) evaluating significant accounting estimates and assessing risks of material misstatement, and (b) assembling information to resolve exceptions in confirmation replies.
• CA P accepted a tax audit and started it within two days without writing to the previous tax auditor. Realising this, he sent a registered letter and got the postal acknowledgement before signing the report.
• CA O received the 'Best Speaker of the Year' award from the Institute and posted a framed photograph of it on his website.
• PQR Co-operative Society offers the firm its statutory audit. Fee options: (i) a percentage of net profits, or (ii) ₹9,501.

morning.question: Q1. On CA Tom's direct assistance, which is correct as per SA 610?
options: Not for (a) estimates and risk assessment; he may help with (b) assembling information
He may help with (a) only, not (b)
He may help with both (a) and (b)
He may help with neither (a) nor (b)
morning.explanation: SA 610: internal auditors cannot give direct assistance in work needing significant judgment (estimates, assessing RMM). Assembling information for exceptions is allowed.

morning.question: Q2. CA P wrote to the previous tax auditor only after starting the audit (but before signing). Is he guilty?
options: No – the requirement is only for statutory audits
No – he wrote before signing the report
Yes – Clause (8), Part I, Second Schedule
Yes – Clause (8), Part I, First Schedule: communication must be BEFORE accepting
morning.explanation: Clause (8) requires written communication with the previous auditor before ACCEPTING the appointment. Writing later does not cure it.

morning.question: Q3. CA O posted his award photograph (award from the Institute) on his website. He is liable under:
options: Clause (9), Part I, First Schedule
Clause (6), Part I, First Schedule
Clause (8), Part I, Second Schedule
Clause (7), Part I, Second Schedule
morning.explanation: Website guidelines bar awards and achievements (except those from Central/State Govt or regulators) and event photographs – a form of solicitation under Clause (6).

morning.question: Q4. For the co-operative society's audit, which fee option can the firm choose?
options: (i) only
Neither (i) nor (ii)
Either (i) or (ii)
(ii) only
morning.explanation: Regulation 192 allows a co-operative society auditor's fee to be based on a percentage of capital, income or profits. A fixed fee is also fine. So either.
